title: John Rush: directory ideas, micro-influencer buying, and selling validated startup drafts
summary: John Rush explains why growth tools beat build tools, how to pick ideas by asking how you'd sell them, and why directories are underrated. He shares a keyword-gap method for validating directories and how he buys micro-influencer posts for $100-300.

principles.text: Building is easy; growth is the scarce skill, so build tools around growth and marketing.
principles.quote: it's easy to build stuff but it's not easy to grow like that's kind of like 99% of the makers can build stuff but only few can actually grow and sell and bring in customers

principles.text: Start ideas from how you'd sell them: watch what people ask for, then wrap the steps into a one-job micro tool.
principles.quote: I think the best way to come up with the idea is to start with how would you sell it so basically uh don't build stuff but just see what people are actually looking for

principles.text: Single-purpose tools are easy to remember and recommend in threads where people ask how to do X.
principles.quote: if tool just only does one thing then it's easy for the user to remember this tool and to recommend that tool comparing to the tools doing like a lot of things

principles.text: Validate directories with a technical test: find a high-traffic keyword with no directory on page one of Google, then build one.
principles.quote: find keyword with high traffic search for it if it doesn't have any directory on the first page of Google go and build it and you can do that for 10 ideas like it's cheap it's fast

principles.text: Copy working English directories into other languages and countries where none exist.
principles.quote: find the directory that's working really well in us uh and just find a country where there is no directory like that and it's easy to find you Just Google like the best thing about directories is that the whole research is in Google

principles.text: Buy micro-influencer posts, bargain down, and become a repeat buyer to get lower fixed prices.
principles.quote: usually they start with really high price so you would get like you know 700 or 800 at the start uh and you should just bargain that down to few hundred and and that usually works even if they say no
